files.migration_notes: Global CSS with class/id selectors used by jQuery. Move to src/styles.css and import in App.jsx. No logic changes needed; keep all rules. Ensure class names (e.g., .completed, .task-text) match React component output.

Replace jQuery script tags with React entry point. Remove and . Add
as mount point. Link Vite entry script: . Keep CSS link updated to new path if needed (e.g., ).

Convert entire jQuery logic to a single React functional component. Replace $(document).ready with useEffect([]). State: tasks[] (from AJAX), showingCompletedOnly (bool). Replace appendTask with TaskItem sub-component (defined in same file) mapping over tasks. Event handlers: onAddClick, onDelete, onToggleComplete, onFilterToggle, onClearCompleted become useState setters. AJAX -> useEffect fetch in useEffect with fetch. Update stats via derived values (tasks.length, filter). Toggle filter updates showingCompletedOnly and conditionally renders items. Clear completed filters tasks. All DOM manipulation replaced by JSX rendering. Import './styles.css' at top.

IMPORTANT: The migrated stylesheet is already imported globally by the app's entry point (main.jsx). Do NOT add any CSS import statement to this file yourself, and do not reference any CSS filename directly in this file.

overall_notes: Migration follows a bottom-up order: styles first, then HTML template, then main component. Risk: single-file constraint forces all React logic into App.jsx, including sub-components, which may become large but avoids cross-file import coordination. Use Vite conventions (no PUBLIC_URL, env vars with VITE_ prefix). Ensure main.jsx renders <App /> into #root. Test fetch against JSONPlaceholder API. No TypeScript; keep JSX in .jsx files.
